title.value: Interpolated Adversarial Training: Achieving robust neural networks without sacrificing too much accuracy
title.justification: The title accurately reflects the innovative training technique proposed in the paper.
title.quote: We propose Interpolated Adversarial Training, which employs recently proposed interpolation based training methods in the framework of adversarial training.

analysis.description: This paper introduces and analyzes Interpolated Adversarial Training (IAT), a technique to enhance the robustness of neural networks against adversarial attacks while maintaining generalization on unperturbed data. The method combines adversarial training with interpolation techniques like Mixup to improve accuracy and robustness efficiently.

type.justification: The paper involves experiments with neural networks, comparing the performance and robustness of models when using Interpolated Adversarial Training.
type.quote: We demonstrate that our approach substantially improves standard test error while still achieving adversarial robustness, using benchmark datasets (CIFAR10, CIFAR100 and SHVN) and benchmark architectures (Wide-ResNet and ResNet): Section 5.1.

name.justification: The paper's main focus is on improving adversarial training techniques to enhance model robustness.
name.quote: Adversarial robustness has become a central goal in deep learning, both in the theory and the practice.

name.justification: The paper combines adversarial training with interpolation-based methods like Mixup, making it a key sub-field.
name.quote: We propose to augment the adversarial training with the interpolation based training, as a solution to the above problem.

name.justification: Wide-ResNet is used as a benchmark architecture in the experiments.
name.quote: We used two architectures : First, the WideResNet architecture proposed in He, Zhang, Ren, and Sun (2015), Zagoruyko and Komodakis (2016) and used in Madry et al. (2017) for adversarial training ^{2}.
